blueprint_topic: Management of Care — collaborative healthcare outbreak investigation
stem: Several similar healthcare-associated infections are identified on one unit. The RN is participating with infection-prevention and public-health personnel in the response. Which investigation plan is most appropriate?

options.A: Verify the diagnoses and outbreak, alert key partners, define and find cases, analyze person-place-time patterns, test hypotheses, and implement control measures as evidence develops.
options.B: Start control measures around the suspected source, then postpone case definition and systematic case finding until the initial measures have been evaluated.
options.C: Verify diagnoses and count known cases, then wait for a confirmed source before alerting additional partners or changing infection-control measures.
options.D: Use facility surveillance and laboratory data to develop a hypothesis, then broaden collaboration after analytic testing identifies the likely source.

rationale: A is correct. CDC's Field Epidemiology Manual describes healthcare outbreak investigation as a systematic process that includes verifying the diagnosis, confirming the outbreak, alerting key partners, establishing case definitions, identifying and counting cases, organizing data by person, place, and time, formulating and testing hypotheses, assessing infection control, implementing control measures, and communicating findings. CDC also notes that control measures may be appropriate at any point and can be modified as evidence evolves. B is incorrect because early control measures can be appropriate, but they do not justify postponing systematic case definition and case finding. C is incorrect because collaboration and reasonable control measures need not wait for definitive source confirmation. D is incorrect because early collaboration with facility, laboratory, infection-prevention, and public-health partners is part of effective investigation rather than something deferred until analytic testing is complete.
educational_objective: Participate in healthcare outbreak response as a systematic, collaborative process that verifies the problem, finds and analyzes cases, tests hypotheses, and implements evidence-informed control measures without delaying appropriate early collaboration or prevention actions.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual — Healthcare Settings; Conducting a Field Investigation; Developing Interventions
source_version_date: Healthcare Settings page dated August 8, 2024; Conducting a Field Investigation dated January 6, 2025; current CDC pages accessed 2026-08-20
source_locator: Healthcare Settings — Field Investigation, Steps 1–10: verify diagnosis; confirm HAI outbreak; alert key partners; establish case definitions; identify/count cases; organize person/place/time/size data; conduct targeted observations; formulate/test hypotheses; perform infection-control assessment and implement control measures; follow up and communicate findings. Developing Interventions — Levels of Certainty: preliminary control measures may be warranted at any step and can be modified as the investigation proceeds. Initiating/Healthcare Settings material emphasizes early collaboration with facility staff, laboratories, IPC, and public health.
source_claim_supported: Healthcare outbreak investigation is a systematic and collaborative process of verification, case definition/finding, descriptive analysis, hypothesis development/testing, control measures, and communication; appropriate early control and collaboration need not await final source confirmation.

correction_summary: Reframed the stem to make the RN's collaborative Management of Care role explicit. Rebuilt distractors to remove absolute-word and answer-length cueing and to test realistic errors involving premature anchoring, delayed partner notification/control, and delayed collaboration.

option_audit.A: Correct; captures CDC's systematic investigation sequence while allowing control measures to evolve with evidence.
option_audit.B: Plausible early-control misconception; incorrect because early empiric measures do not replace prompt case definition and case finding.
option_audit.C: Plausible certainty-threshold error; incorrect because partner alert and appropriate controls need not await definitive source confirmation.
option_audit.D: Plausible analytic-sequencing error; incorrect because effective investigation relies on early multidisciplinary collaboration rather than delayed collaboration after hypothesis testing.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/all/only/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All options carry comparable procedural detail and the key is not uniquely identifiable by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options are parallel investigation plans within the same construct.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified. B, C, and D each omit or delay a CDC-described core investigation activity.
